Synthesis of sphingolipids, which include sphingomyelin, ceramides, cerebrosides, and gangliosides, begins by the condensa-
tion of palmitoyl-CoA (16:0-CoA) with serine. The amino group of serine is then acylated by a second fatty acyl-CoA to form ceram-
ide; the chain length of the second FA can be variable. Transfer of phosphorylcholine (from phosphatidylcholine) to the hydroxyl
group of ceramide yields sphingomyelin. Alternatively, sugars (from sugar nucleotide donors) are added to produce the cerebro-
sides, gangliosides, and related lipids.
